paper.title_en: Electron-electron interactions mediated by vibrations: Implications for chirality-induced spin selectivity
paper.abstract_en: Molecular vibrations that modulate both electronic hopping and spin--orbit coupling (SOC) have been proposed as an ingredient of chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS). We study a four-site bridge coupled to a single Peierls mode that modulates both terms, with amplitudes $g$ and $χ$. An exact Lang--Firsov transformation yields the transformed Hamiltonian in closed form; in the antiadiabatic limit, it reduces to a purely fermionic model with instantaneous vibration-mediated interactions, whose two-body part separates into $g^2$, $χ^2$, and $gχ$ channels, the last containing a Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interaction (DMI) and correlated hopping. For a common SOC axis, local spin rotations mix these channels, so that the DMI is not separately gauge invariant; the invariant content lies in the components $g_\parallel$ and $g_\perp$ of the Peierls coupling parallel and perpendicular to the static bond. For spin-independent injection and extraction, the acceptor polarization $P_A$ is odd in both components, vanishes on two nodal lines, and reverses with the handedness of the bridge. We also prove that, for a common SOC axis and a single irreversible exit, a single electron transferred through an empty bridge acquires no long-time polarization, at any coupling strength. Donor--bridge--acceptor simulations with a half-filled bridge and the mode treated explicitly obey the symmetry rule. At weak coupling, $P_A$ scales as $g_\parallel g_\perp\simeq gχ$, and, for the transfer rates considered, on-site Coulomb repulsion enhances it by a factor of about three. Within the model, a long-time polarization of the transferred charge is thus a many-electron effect: it requires spin exchange between the transferred electron and the other bridge electrons.
